source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: You are exempt from obtaining a Hawaii drivers license when you are employed by the federal government and driving a federally owned motor vehicle that is not a commercial motor vehicle while holding a valid drivers license issued by a federal agency.
corrections.note: Added the missing requirement that you be employed by the federal government.

corrections.corrected_statement: A provisional license comes at sixteen after the permit period, while a class three license requires age seventeen and completion of the graduated program for anyone under eighteen.
corrections.note: The provisional age requirement is stated on page thirteen not the cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: The permit-holding requirement is one hundred eighty days, while the provisional-holding requirement before class three is six months.
corrections.note: The one hundred eighty day permit requirement is stated on page thirteen.

corrections.corrected_statement: A REAL ID compliant license works as federal identification, while a limited purpose license allows driving only and proves nothing for federal purposes, employment, voting or benefits.
corrections.note: The REAL ID federal identification use is stated on page eleven.

corrections.corrected_statement: Anyone applying for a new REAL ID compliant license or permit must provide documents proving legal name and date of birth and legal presence and social security number and two documents proving Hawaii principal residence.
corrections.note: Removed the added claim that each other category needs one separate document.

corrections.corrected_statement: Class one covers mopeds and class two covers motorcycles, and each needs its own knowledge and off-street skills tests, while class three is the car license.
corrections.note: The class three age requirement is stated on page twelve.

corrections.corrected_statement: You must hold a provisional license for six months before applying for a drivers license and the page leaves the minimum age blank.
corrections.note: Cited page states the hold but leaves the age blank.

corrections.corrected_statement: Class three covers any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of eighteen thousand pounds or less, vehicles designed to carry fifteen or fewer passengers including the driver, and autocycles.
corrections.note: Autocycle rule appears on page fifteen not fourteen.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state rules for applying for a duplicate license.
corrections.note: No duplicate license text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state rules for reporting a residence address change.
corrections.note: No address change text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state rules for reporting a change of name.
corrections.note: No name change text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state rules about medical conditions or driving privilege.
corrections.note: No medical fitness text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state rules about medical reports vision tests or restricted licenses.
corrections.note: No medical report text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state when a drivers license is withdrawn or restricted.
corrections.note: No withdrawal text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state letter codes for license restrictions.
corrections.note: No letter restriction text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state numbered codes for license restrictions.
corrections.note: No numbered restriction text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state rules for reporting address changes or name changes.
corrections.note: No address or name text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: The provided pages do not state letter or numbered codes for restrictions.
corrections.note: No restriction code text on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: All motor vehicles operated on public highways must have an official periodic motor vehicle inspection at least once a year, except ambulances must be inspected once every six months and new vehicles do not need to be inspected until two years after they are first sold.
corrections.note: Added missing exceptions for ambulances and new vehicles.

corrections.corrected_statement: If the directional signals fail, use hand signals until you can have them repaired.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported claim about brake lamps and head lamps.

corrections.corrected_statement: Any driving situation involves the environment and your vehicle and you as the driver, and only you can gather information and apply skill knowledge experience and judgment and take action to safely complete the driving task.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported claim that environment and vehicle are conditions the driver must manage.

corrections.corrected_statement: You must drive on the right half of the roadway where opposite direction vehicles pass on the right and narrow roads leave oncoming vehicles at least half of the main traveled portion, and when moving slower than other traffic you should drive in the extreme right lane.
corrections.note: Changed must to should for slower traffic in extreme right lane.

corrections.corrected_statement: You may pass on the right of a vehicle about to make a left turn without driving off the pavement or main traveled portion of the roadway, and you may also pass on the right on a paved street or highway with two or more lanes marked for traffic in each direction or on a one way street with two or more lanes marked for traffic.
corrections.note: Changed your direction to in each direction for multilane passing on right.

corrections.corrected_statement: Funeral processions and convoys have the right of way at intersections with vehicles usually using headlamps for identification and the first and last vehicles usually having a distinctive marking, and you should not drive your vehicle between the vehicles in a funeral procession.
corrections.note: Changed must not to should not for driving between procession vehicles.

corrections.corrected_statement: Passing is banned within one hundred feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, while a hill or curve requires seven hundred to one thousand feet of clear distance before passing.
corrections.note: Statement is correct but hill curve distance is on page 30 not 31.

corrections.corrected_statement: Yield to the car on the right when vehicles approach at the same time and yield to all oncoming traffic that is so close as to be a hazard when turning left.
corrections.note: Removed regardless of arrival wording not stated on page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left or when two or more lanes run your way, while passing on the right shoulder is never allowed.
corrections.note: Statement is correct but shoulder ban is on page 30 not 26.

corrections.corrected_statement: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is an eighteen-inch reflective triangle for vehicles built for twenty-five miles per hour or less, while the no passing zone pennant is a yellow sign on the left side of the road.
corrections.note: Statement is correct but pennant rule is on page 31 not 30.

corrections.corrected_statement: After stopping and yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles, you may turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it, and you may turn left on red only from a one way street into a one way street where traffic is moving to the left unless a sign prohibits it.
corrections.note: Added stop and yield requirements and left turn traffic direction limit and removed any street.

corrections.corrected_statement: A red X lane control signal means the lane belongs to opposing traffic, while a red arrow means stop for that lane just as a red light would.
corrections.note: Red arrow rule is printed on page forty, not page forty-one.

corrections.corrected_statement: A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, while a right turn on red requires yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles.
corrections.note: Right on red yield rule is printed on page thirty-nine, not page forty.

corrections.corrected_statement: A crash must be reported to police at three thousand dollars of property damage, while a bodily-injury lawsuit becomes possible at five thousand dollars of medical bills.
corrections.note: The three thousand dollar reporting rule is stated on page 52, not page 54.

corrections.corrected_statement: Non-compliance with the safety responsibility law costs the driver's license by suspension, while non-compliance with the insurance law can also cost the vehicle's registration certificate.
corrections.note: The registration forfeiture penalty is stated on page 54, not page 53.

corrections.corrected_statement: The adult threshold for administrative revocation is point zero eight, while the zero tolerance threshold for drivers under twenty-one is point zero two.
corrections.note: The point zero eight admin-revocation rule is on page 55, not the cited page 56.

corrections.corrected_statement: A failed test and a refused test both trigger administrative revocation with a thirty-day temporary permit, while refusal adds a one, two or four year revocation based on prior alcohol enforcement contacts.
corrections.note: The one, two or four year refusal periods are on page 56, not the cited page 55.

corrections.corrected_statement: Keep at least a two second following gap behind the vehicle ahead measured by counting one thousand one one thousand two from a roadside marker and never follow with less.
corrections.note: Removed rear-tires stopping gap because no provided page states it.

corrections.corrected_statement: Hazard flashers warn of a vehicle stopped in a hazardous position and are never used while moving, while turn signals are used for every turn and lane change while moving.
corrections.note: The every-turn-or-lane-change rule is stated on page 74, not the cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Parallel parking starts eighteen inches from the front car and ends with bumpers at least two feet from the neighbors, while the curbside wheels must finish within twelve inches of the curb.

Complete steering failure almost never happens on a well-maintained vehicle, but a partial loss can occur with power steering, in which case you must apply greater effort to the wheel and never give up on steering.
corrections.note: The never give up instruction appears on page 82, not page 81.

corrections.corrected_statement: A missed freeway exit means continuing to the next exit, while needing the opposite direction means leaving at the next exit and re-entering, never crossing the divider or turning around.
corrections.note: The missed exit rule appears on page 80, not page 79.

corrections.corrected_statement: At dawn and dusk turn on low beam headlamps so others can see you, and at night if oncoming lights are too bright flash high beams once and look at the right edge of the road while using lane markings as a guide.
corrections.note: Right edge glance applies only to bright oncoming lights, not to dawn and dusk.

corrections.corrected_statement: Research shows that over two thirds of car and motorcycle crashes result from the car driver turning in front of the motorcyclist.
corrections.note: Removed the unsupported claim that intersections are where the turn most often happens.

corrections.corrected_statement: When a registered owner's address changes from the one on the registration application, the owner must notify the county agency in writing within thirty days, giving the old and new addresses, the vehicle license number, the make and the vehicle identification number.
corrections.note: Details continue on page 22, not page 21.

corrections.corrected_statement: A temporary permit runs until the out-of-state registration expires but never beyond twelve months, while a Hawaii registration expires at the end of its own twelfth month every year.
corrections.note: Annual expiry is stated on page 21, not page 23.

corrections.corrected_statement: A new vehicle from another state needs a manufacturer's certificate of origin or a notarized bill of sale, while a used vehicle from another state needs the title, the registration and a notarized bill of sale from the named seller.
corrections.note: Used-vehicle rule is stated on page 23, not page 22.

corrections.corrected_statement: A single solid white line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances with great care, while a double solid white line may never be crossed.
Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

The two-way left turn lane is open to vehicles from both directions for left turns only, while double solid yellow lines without such a lane allow crossing only for a left turn into a driveway or alley.
Railroad crossing pavement markings are white with a yellow no-passing centerline, while red pavement markings mean a roadway must not be entered at all.

Yellow indicates a warning of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond shaped sign, while orange indicates a warning concerning road work and appears on rectangular or diamond shaped signs.
corrections.note: Added almost always qualifier for yellow diamond shape.

corrections.corrected_statement: Do not pass signs indicate locations where you must not pass on two or three lane roads, while the yellow and black pennant on the left side of the road points to the beginning of the no passing zone.
corrections.note: Corrected beginning of zone to pennant sign, not do not pass sign.

corrections.corrected_statement: An exclusion sign uses a red circle, with or without a diagonal slash, to prohibit a movement or activity, while other regulatory signs use black or red lettering on white to state restrictions in words.
corrections.note: Second clause about other regulatory signs is on page 47 not page 46.

corrections.corrected_statement: Guide and information signs in green, blue or brown locate places and services, while warning signs in yellow describe hazards.
corrections.note: Color details are on page 43 not page 48.

corrections.corrected_statement: A driver passing a bicyclist must keep at least three feet of space until safely past.
corrections.note: Removed parked-car door clause not on cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: A pedestrian should wait for the next green cycle when the green light has been showing for some time.
corrections.note: Removed close-vehicles clause not on cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: A pedestrian walks on the left side facing traffic, while a bicyclist rides on the right side with traffic.

The inattentive driver drives with one arm out the window, gestures while talking to passengers, pays little attention to traffic, daydreams or gazes off the road when alone, and forfeits safety through that inattention.
corrections.note: The one arm phrase is on page fifty seven not page fifty eight.

corrections.corrected_statement: Wear the lap shoulder belt low and snug and have the baby ride in a car safety seat such as an infant seat or a convertible seat in the infant or toddler position and never carry the baby in your arms.
corrections.note: Removed before birth mother claim not on the page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Use an infant seat or a convertible seat in the infant position and do not face an infant forward.
corrections.note: Removed rearward which the page does not state.
